# I. Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for type (combined) with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5)
```{r}
prior_beta_type <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.5, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: NONE.  Howvever, add centre as improves regularisation.




## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_type <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ type
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 15, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_type,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```



## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_type)
```



## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_type)
```



## Model short summary
```{r}

```


## Check model performance
### 1. Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_type) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```





### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_type_prior_only <- update(mod_type, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_type_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```








### 3. Check posterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_type)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_type_prior_only)
```



#### b. type_intermediate
##### i. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "typeintermediate"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Neutral prior vs posterior for intermediate type", xlab = "Beta coefficient for intermediate type", xlim = c(-2, 3),  ylim = c(0, 1.4)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "typeintermediate"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```





##### ii. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "typeintermediate"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "typeintermediate"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "typeintermediate"] - mean(prior_draws[, "typeintermediate"])))

```






#### c. type_b
##### i. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
```{r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "typeb"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Neutral prior vs posterior for type B", xlab = "Beta coefficient for type B", xlim = c(-2, 3), ylim = c(0, 1.4)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "typeb"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



##### ii. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "typeb"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "typeb"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "typeb"] - mean(prior_draws[, "typeb"])))

```




### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for type variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = FALSE),
  main = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ type 
            + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 5, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for type_intermediate across different priors
##### i. type_intermediate
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio for type_intermediate across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(typeintermediate, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio for type_intermediate across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "typeintermediate", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```







##### ii. type_b
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio for type_intermediate across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(typeb, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio for type_b across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "typeb", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```



Text for paper:
"Prior–likelihood compatibility was assessed using prior predictive checks and by comparing prior and posterior marginal distributions of key parameters. Sensitivity analyses were performed by refitting models under weaker and stronger priors; substantive conclusions were robust to these choices.”





## Make model predictions and plot
### 1. Create new data where type differs
```{r}
nd1 <- data.frame(type = c("a", "b", "intermediate"),
                 centre = c("p", "p", "p"))
head(nd1)
```




#### 2. Make posterior predictions from new data
```{r}
ps <- posterior_survfit(mod_type,
  newdata = nd1,
  times = 0,
  extrapolate = TRUE) |>
  suppressWarnings()
head(ps)
```




#### 3. Plot
```{r}
panel_labels <- c('1' = "Type A", '2' = "Type B", '3' = "Intermediate type")
pps <- plot(ps) +
  aes(colour = factor(id), fill = factor(id)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels)) +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=12, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               title = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 10),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 10)) +
            theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold.italic"),
                    strip.background = element_rect(fill="white") ) +
            scale_colour_hue(h.start = 120) +
            scale_fill_hue(h.start = 120)
        
print(pps)
```



## Check PH assumption visually
### make predictions of both the hazard and log hazard
```{r}
ph <- suppressWarnings( posterior_survfit(mod_type, newdata = nd1, type = "haz") )
pl <- suppressWarnings( posterior_survfit(mod_type, newdata = nd1, type = "loghaz") )
```




#### create plots
```{r}
pph <- plot(ph) +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels))
ppl <- plot(pl) +
  facet_wrap(~ id, labeller = labeller(id = panel_labels))
```




#### combine plots in grid and plot

# II. Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for s_age with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_age <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.25, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: NONE.  However, add centre as improves regularisation.




## Fit model with for s_age
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_age <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_age
                     + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 15, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_age,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```

## Check model performance
### 1.Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_age) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```



### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_age_prior_only <- update(mod_age, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_age_prior_only)  |>
  suppressWarnings()
```





### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_age)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_age_prior_only)
```





#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "s_age"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Neutral prior vs posterior for age", xlab = "Beta coefficient for effect of age", xlim = c(-1, 1) ) 
dens(prior_draws[, "s_age"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```


#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "s_age"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_age"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "s_age"] - mean(prior_draws[, "s_age"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_age variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.25, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 0.625, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```





#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_age
            + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```




#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios for age across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_age, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_age", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# VI.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of NFD (s_vtiao_vtipv) with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_nfd <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.5, autoscale = TRUE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: pressure grad, referral centre.





## Fit model with for s_vtiao_vtipv
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_nfd <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_vtiao_vtipv
                       + s_pv_max_pg
                       + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 15, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_nfd,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```




## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_nfd)
```



## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_nfd)
```



## Model short summary
```{r}
print(mod_nfd, digits = 3)
```



## Plot Baseline hazard of model
```{r}
plot(mod_nfd)
```



## Plots of model convergences

## Get results
```{r}
posterior_mod_nfd <- as.array(mod_nfd)
```

```{r}

mcmc_trace(posterior_mod_nfd)
```



### b. Trace rank plot
```{r}

mcmc_rank_overlay(posterior_mod_nfd) +
  ylim(c(325, 500))
```



### c. get dens overlay plot for chains
```{r}
color_scheme_set("blue")
mcmc_dens_overlay(posterior_mod_nfd)
```



## Summaries of coefficients

### a. HPDI for the different beta parameters
```{r}
draws <- as.matrix(mod_nfd)
median(draws[,2]) # draws for s_vtiao_vtipv
HPDI(draws[,2], 0.97) # draws for s_vtiao_vtipv
HPDI(draws[,2], 0.89) # draws for s_vtiao_vtipv
```



### b. Hypothesis tests on beta parameters
#### s_vtiao_vtipv
probability that effect is positive
```{r}
mean(draws[,2] > 0) # draws for s_vtiao_vtipv
```



### c. Plot posterior distribution for beta coefficient of s_vtiao_vtipv
```{r}
s_nfd <- draws[,2] # 2nd column is draws for s_vtiao_vtipv

ggplot(data.frame(s_nfd), aes(x = s_nfd)) +
  geom_density(fill = "orange", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Posterior of beta coefficient for Ao VTI / P VTI",
       x = "Beta coefficient",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=16, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               title = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 12),

                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5) +
  xlim(-1, 1) +
  ylim(0, 3)
```







## Get HDI for coefficients

```{r}
plot(hdi)
```




## Get area plot for posterior distributons of beta parameters




## Calculate hazard ratios for s_vtiao_vtipv
### a. get posterior draws
```{r}
s_vtiao_vtipv_hr <- exp(draws[,2]) # draws for s_vtiao_vtipv)
```



### b. Summarise hazard ratios for s_vtiao_vtipv
```{r}
median(s_vtiao_vtipv_hr)
hpdi_s_vtiao_vtipv_hr <- HPDI(s_vtiao_vtipv_hr, prob = c(0.89, 0.97))
hpdi_s_vtiao_vtipv_hr
```



### c. Plot posterior distribution for hazard ratio of s_vtiao_vtipv
```{r}
ggplot(data.frame(s_vtiao_vtipv_hr), aes(x = s_vtiao_vtipv_hr)) +
  geom_density(fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Posterior distribution of hazard ratio for Ao VTI / P VTI",
       x = "Hazard Ratio",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=12, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               title = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 12),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 12)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype="dotted", 
                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5) +
  xlim(0, 2.0) +
  ylim(0, 2.5)
```



## Check model performance
### 1. Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_nfd) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```



### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_nfd_prior_only <- update(mod_nfd, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_nfd_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```






### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_nfd)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_nfd_prior_only)
```



#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "s_vtiao_vtipv"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for Ao VTI / P VTI", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of VTI_AO : VTI_PV", xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(0, 3)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "s_vtiao_vtipv"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "s_vtiao_vtipv"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_vtiao_vtipv"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "s_vtiao_vtipv"] - mean(prior_draws[, "s_vtiao_vtipv"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vtiao_vtipv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 5, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.25, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_vtiao_vtipv
            + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios acxross different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_vtiao_vtipv, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_vtiao_vtipv", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

```{r}
                 )
head(nd)
```

```{r}
print(pps)
```

# X.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of RIGHT CHF with random intercept for centre

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5)
```{r}
prior_beta_chf <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0, autoscale = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: RV syst dys, arrhyth, concurrent congen, pressure grad, referral centre, stenosis type





## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_chf <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ chf
                     + concurrent_congenital
                     + type
                     + s_tapse
                     + s_pv_max_pg
                     + arrhythmias
                     + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 12.5, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_chf,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```



## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_chf)
```



## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_chf)
```




## Model short summary
```{r}
print(mod_chf, digits = 3)
```



## Plot Baseline hazard of model
```{r}
plot(mod_chf)
```



## Plots of model convergences

## Get results
```{r}
posterior_mod_chf <- as.array(mod_chf)
```

```{r}

mcmc_trace(posterior_mod_chf)
```



### b. Trace rank plot
```{r}

mcmc_rank_overlay(posterior_mod_chf) +
  ylim(325, 500)
```



### c. get dens overlay plot for chains
```{r}
color_scheme_set("blue")
mcmc_dens_overlay(posterior_mod_chf)
```



## Summaries of coefficients

### HPDI for the different beta parameters

```{r}
draws <- as.matrix(mod_chf)
median(draws[,2]) # draws for chf
HPDI(draws[,2], 0.97) # draws for chf
HPDI(draws[,2], 0.89) # draws for chf
```



### Hypothesis tests on beta parameters
#### chf
probability that effect is positive
```{r}
mean(draws[,2] > 0) # draws for chf
```



### c. Plot posterior distribution for beta coefficient of chf
```{r}
s_arr <- draws[,2] # 2nd column is draws for chf

ggplot(data.frame(s_arr), aes(x = s_arr)) +
  geom_density(fill = "orange", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Posterior distribution of beta coefficient for right CHF",
       x = "Beta coefficient",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=16, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               title = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 12),

  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype="dotted", 
                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5) +
  xlim(-1, 4) +
  ylim(0, 0.9)
```






## Get HDI for coefficients

```{r}
plot(hdi)
```




## Calculate hazard ratios for chf
### a. get posterior draws
```{r}
chf_hr <- exp(draws[,2]) # 2nd column is draws for chf)
```



### b. Summarise hazard ratios for chf
```{r}
median(chf_hr)
hpdi_chf_hr <- HPDI(chf_hr, prob = c(0.89, 0.97))
hpdi_chf_hr
```



### c. Plot posterior distribution for hazard ratio of chf
```{r}
ggplot(data.frame(chf_hr), aes(x = chf_hr)) +
  geom_density(fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Posterior distribution of hazard ratio for right CHF",
       x = "Hazard Ratio",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_bw() +
           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=12, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               title = element_text(size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 12),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey8",size = 12)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype="dotted", 
                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5) +
  xlim(0, 10)
```




## Check model performance
### 1. Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_chf) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```




### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_chf_prior_only <- update(mod_chf, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_chf_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```







### 3. Check posterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_chf)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_chf_prior_only)
```





#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "chf1"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Neutral prior vs posterior for right CHF", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of right CHF", xlim = c(-1, 4), ylim = c(0, 0.9)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "chf1"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```





#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "chf1"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "chf1"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "chf1"] - mean(prior_draws[, "chf1"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4.0, autoscale = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE)),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0, autoscale = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE)),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.0, autoscale = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ chf
                     + concurrent_congenital
                     + type
                     + s_tapse
                     + s_pv_max_pg
                     + arrhythmias
                     + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios acxross different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(chf1, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "chf1", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# XII.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of ATENOLOL with random intercept for centre and control set

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_aten <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE))
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: RV syst dys, referral centre.



## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_aten <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ atenolol
                      + s_tapse
                      + surgery
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_aten,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.99999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
  init = 0.1,  seed = 666)
```



## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_aten)
```



## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_aten)
```



## Model short summary
```{r}
print(mod_aten, digits = 3)
```





## Check model performance
### 1. Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_aten) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```



### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_aten_prior_only <- update(mod_aten, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_aten_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```

# XIV.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of COMPLICATIONS with random intercept for centre and control set

## Set prior for beta variables
Set a neutral, weakly-regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0)
```{r}
prior_beta_comp <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: high pressure, low pressure, referral centre, stent.
NB need to include balloon type here as well for an appropriate adjustment set




## Need to create separate variables for high pressure and low pressure so as to model complications appropriately
```{r}
df_surg$high_pressure <- ifelse(df_surg$balloon_type == "high_pressure", 1, 0)
df_surg$high_pressure[is.na(df_surg$high_pressure)] <- 0
df_surg$low_pressure <- ifelse(df_surg$balloon_type == "low_pressure", 1, 0)
df_surg$low_pressure[is.na(df_surg$low_pressure)] <- 0
```




## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_comp <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ complications
                      + stent
                      + high_pressure
                      + low_pressure
                      + (1| centre),
  data = df_surg,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 15, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_beta_comp,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```





## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_comp)
```



## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_comp)
```



## Model short summary
```{r}
print(mod_comp, digits = 3)
```





## Check model performance
### 1. Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_comp) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```



### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_comp_prior_only <- update(mod_comp, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_comp_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```

## Check model performance
### check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_cong) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```



### 1. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_cong_prior_only <- update(mod_cong, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_cong_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```





### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_cong)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_cong_prior_only)
```





#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "concurrent_congenital1"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for concurrent congenital disease", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of concurrent congenital disease", xlim = c(-0.5, 2.5)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "concurrent_congenital1"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "concurrent_congenital1"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "concurrent_congenital1"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "concurrent_congenital1"] - mean(prior_draws[, "concurrent_congenital1"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for concurrent congenital variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ concurrent_congenital
                      + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios across different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(concurrent_congenital1, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "concurrent_congenital1", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```












## Make model predictions and plot for mod_cong
### 1. Create new data where concurrent congenital differs

```{r}
                 concurrent_congenital = c(0, 1)
                 )
head(nd)
```

```{r}
            theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold.italic"),

        )
print(pps)
```

To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ clinical_signs
                         + chf
                         + arrhythmias
                         + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios acxross different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(clinical_signs, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "clinical_signs", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# XVII.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of BALLOON TYPE with random intercept for centre
Have conditioned on balloon use... by using the df_balloon dataset which only includes dogs that had a balloon procedure.  This conditions on surgery (only including those that had a procedure, and then use of balloon in procedure_type) Therefore, no control set required (other than including centre as a grouping variable) for the causal effect to be estimated.

## Neutral prior for clinicial signs
No prior information on the effect of clinical signs
Therefore, set a Neutral weekly regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5)
```{r}
prior_balloon_type <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.0, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: proc type, referral centre, stenosis type.
NB to include procedure type, simply use df_balloon as that will ensure anaylsis only includes dogs that had a balloon procedure.




## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_balloon_type <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ balloon_type
                              + type
                              + (1| centre),
  data = df_balloon,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 15, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_balloon_type,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```




## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_balloon_type)
```




## Model summary
```{r}
summary(mod_balloon_type)
```




## Model short summary
```{r}
print(mod_balloon_type, digits = 3)
```





## Check model performance
### 1.  Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_balloon_type) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```






### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_balloon_type_prior_only <- update(mod_balloon_type, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_balloon_type_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```

### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}

prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_rsdysn_prior_only)
```




#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "s_tapse_n"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Neutral prior v posterior for TAPSE", xlab = "Beta coefficient for effect of TAPSE", xlim = c(-1.5, 0.5)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "s_tapse_n"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "s_tapse_n"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_tapse_n"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "s_tapse_n"] - mean(prior_draws[, "s_tapse_n"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_tapse_n variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 5, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.25, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE))
)
```





#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_tapse_n
                       + s_pv_max_pg
                       + type
                       + (1| centre),
            data = df,
            basehaz = "ms",
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```




#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios acxross different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_tapse_n, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_tapse_n", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

```{r}
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 12),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 12)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype="dotted", 
                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5) +
  xlim(0.5, 3.5)
```





## Check model performance
### 1. Check performance of posterior probability
NB equivalent of pp_check
```{r}
ps_check(mod_rvhypn) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```





### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_rvhypn_prior_only <- update(mod_rvhypn, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_rvhypn_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```




### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_rvhypn)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_rvhypn_prior_only)
```




#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "s_ed_rvfw_n"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Comparison of prior and posterior for RVFWd", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of RVFWd", xlim = c(-0.5, 1.5)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "s_ed_rvfw_n"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "s_ed_rvfw_n"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_ed_rvfw_n"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "s_ed_rvfw_n"] - mean(prior_draws[, "s_ed_rvfw_n"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 4, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE))
)
```





#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_ed_rvfw_n
                       + s_vmaxav_vmaxpv
                       + type
                       + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.9999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            seed = 666
            )
})
```





#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios acxross different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_ed_rvfw_n, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_ed_rvfw_n", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

```{r}
  suppressWarnings()
```




### 2. Check performance of prior probability
```{r}
mod_aopv_prior_only <- update(mod_aopv, prior_PD = TRUE)
ps_check(mod_aopv_prior_only) |>
  suppressWarnings()
```




### 3. Check prosterior vs prior for beta variable
#### a. extract draws for posterior and prior
```{r}
# extract draws
post_draws  <- as.matrix(mod_aopv)
prior_draws <- as.matrix(mod_aopv_prior_only)
```





#### b. plot marginal distributions for posterior and prior
``` {r}
# Compare marginal distributions
dens(post_draws[, "s_edao_pvtrunk"], show.zero = TRUE, col = "red", main = "Prior vs posterior for AVa:PVa ratio", xlab = "Beta coefficient for the effect of AVa:PVa ratio", xlim = c(-1.0, 1.0)) 
dens(prior_draws[, "s_edao_pvtrunk"], add=TRUE, col = "blue", show.zero = TRUE)
```



#### c. compute prior tail probability of posterior mean
If this probability is very small (e.g. < 0.05), the posterior lies in a region the prior considered implausible.
```{r}
beta_hat <- mean(post_draws[, "s_edao_pvtrunk"])

mean(abs(prior_draws[, "s_edao_pvtrunk"] - beta_hat) <
       abs(prior_draws[, "s_edao_pvtrunk"] - mean(prior_draws[, "s_edao_pvtrunk"])))

```





### 4. Sensitivity analyses to assess robustness of results to choice of prior
#### a. create priors of different strength for s_vmaxav_vmaxpv variable
To determine whether the substantive conclusions depend upon the exact prior choice.

NB the scale variable is strengthened or weakened by multiplying or dividing the scale of the main prior by 2, respectively. The location is set to the posterior mean from the main model, to ensure that the priors are centred on a plausible value.
NB.  Had to use 0.5, 1, and 2 to ensure that the chains all completed.
```{r}
priors_bin <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2, autoscale = FALSE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1, autoscale = FALSE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 0.5, autoscale = FALSE)
)
```




#### b. refit model with different priors and compare results
```{r}
fits <- lapply(priors_bin, function(p) {
  stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ s_edao_pvtrunk
                       + s_vmaxav_vmaxpv
                       + s_pv_max_pg
                       + s_ed_rvfw
                       + concurrent_congenital
                       + (1| centre),
            basehaz = "ms",
            data = df,
            prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 20, autoscale = FALSE),
            prior = p,
            prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
            iter    = 2000,
            chains = 4,
            cores = 4,
            adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
            control = list(max_treedepth = 20),
            init = 0.1,
            seed = 666
            )
})
```



#### c. compare posterior intervals for hazard ratios acxross different priors
```{r}
# calculate median hazard ratio across different priors
HR_med_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(f) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    summarise(
      median = exp(quantile(s_edao_pvtrunk, probs = 0.5))
    )
})
HR_med <- c(HR_med_sens[[1]], HR_med_sens[[2]], HR_med_sens[[3]])


# calculate 89% credible interval for hazard ratio across different priors
HR_sens <- sapply(fits, function(f) {
  exp(posterior_interval(f, pars = "s_edao_pvtrunk", prob = 0.89))
})

# combine median and credible intervals into a summary table
HR_sens_summary <- rbind(HR_med, HR_sens)
row.names(HR_sens_summary) <- c("Median", "Lower", "Upper")

# transpose the table for better readability
HR_sens_summary
```

# XXII.  Bayesian multi-level survival analysis for effect of annular_hypoplasia with random intercept for centre
No control set required for the causal effect to be estimated.


## Neutral prior for annular_hypoplasia
No prior information on the effect of clinical signs
Therefore, set a Neutral weekly regularising prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 2.5)
```{r}
prior_annular_hypoplasia <- student_t(df = 3, location = 0, scale = 1.5, autoscale = FALSE)
```

Based on the DAG, use the following adjustment variables: Right CHF, arrhyth.  However, also add centre as improves regularisation.




## Fit model
NB use status ... rstanarm requires the dead animals to be classified as 1, whilst censored are 0.
```{r}
mod_annular_hypoplasia <- stan_surv(formula = Surv(time, status) ~ annular_hypoplasia
                         + (1| centre),
  data = df,
  basehaz = "ms",
  prior_intercept = normal(location = 0, scale = 10, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior = prior_annular_hypoplasia,
  prior_covariance =  decov(regularization = 2, concentration = 1, shape = 1, scale = 1),
  iter    = 12000,
  warmup = 4000,
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  adapt_delta = 0.999,  # Often helpful for complex models
  seed = 666)
```





## Summarise priors from model
```{r}
prior_summary(mod_annular_hypoplasia)
```
